hints: Focus on what cold bromine in the dark does to an alkene, it adds two Br atoms across the C=C bond by electrophilic addition.
Draw the dibromo addition product for 1 as $\text{CHBr}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3$ and spot the middle carbon with four different groups.
Now add $\text{Br}_2$ to 2 and 3 and check for four different groups, look for repeated $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ groups or carbons with two identical Br atoms.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Cold bromine in the dark gives electrophilic addition across the C=C bond. One Br adds to each alkene carbon.

$$\text{C=C} + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CBr-CBr}$$

**Draw the three addition products**

Add one Br to each doubly bonded carbon and keep the original Br and alkyl groups.

$$1: \text{CHBr=CHCH}_3 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CHBr}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3$$
$$2: \text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{Br} + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{BrCHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$$
$$3: \text{CH}_2\text{=CBrCH}_3 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{BrCBr}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Test each product for a chiral carbon**

A chiral carbon has four different groups attached. No plane of symmetry and no two identical substituents.

For 1, C-2 is $\text{CHBr(CH}_3\text{)(CHBr}_2\text{)(H)}$. All four are different, so it is chiral. For 2, the middle carbon is $\text{CHBr(CH}_2\text{Br)(CH}_2\text{Br)(H)}$. It has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ groups, so it is achiral. For 3, the product is 1,2,2-tribromopropane. C-1 is $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and C-2 is $\text{CBr}_2$, neither can be chiral.

So only 1 gives a chiral product.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all give chiral products. Only 1 does. Products 2 and 3 have symmetry or repeated groups that prevent chirality.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 both give chiral products. Product 2 is $\text{CH}_2\text{BrCHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$. The central carbon has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ groups, so it is not chiral.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 give chiral products. Product 2 has two identical ends and product 3 is $\text{CH}_2\text{BrCBr}_2\text{CH}_3$ with a $\text{CBr}_2$ carbon, so neither has a carbon with four different groups.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is correct. Addition gives $\text{CHBr}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3$ where C-2 is bonded to H, Br, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CHBr}_2$, four different groups, so it is a chiral centre.
